newsitem.title: Netherlands: FOCUS-Dutch PTT to split itself in two.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dutch PTT to split itself in two.

text.p: Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Tuesday it planned to split itself into two independent post and telecommunications companies by spring 1998 -- a move which had been widely expected by investment analysts.
Its statement did not mention any plans to seek separate stock exchange listings for the two companies but a company spokesman told Reuters this was "quite possible".
The company's share price jumped on the Amsterdam bourse, rising 4.20 guilders or 5.5 percent to 79.90.

PTT Nederland said the move was a logical step following the rapid development of both businesses after a phased privatisation in 1994 and 1995 which has left the Dutch government with a minority holding of some 44 percent.

"Existing and potential synergy effects are not considered crucial to the business strategies of PTT Post and PTT Telecom...The split will widen strategic opportunities and make the valuation of the shares more transparent," it said.
PTT Post, with 1996 sales of 13.5 billion guilders, grabbed the headlines last year with a 2.7 billion guilder takeover of the Australian express delivery service TNT Ltd.
PTT Telecom, with 1996 sales of 14.3 billion guilders, is gearing itself up for the complete liberalisation of its domestic telecommunications market next month.
In the international arena, PTT Telecom has recently announced plans to merge its international networks with those of its partners in the Unisource alliance -- Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT.
PTT Nederland said the splitting of the company would make it easier for PTT Telecom to reinforce international alliances through the mutual acquisition of share capital.
